what_happened: The agent told the person running Athena that the steward's fixes sat at places 364 to 374 in the plan. It had counted the arrows between items in the plan's order line as if they were items. The real places are about 182 to 187 of 203. The fixes are still near the end of the queue, so the finding holds. No job work was judged bad. The agent corrected itself.
cause: A person or agent reports on state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it. Here the state was the plan's queue position. The plan is shown only as a raw order line, with separators mixed in with the item ids, and Athena offers no per-item position view. Position is worked out by hand from raw text, and the agent's own promise to check is the only guard.
prevention: A code check: a status command that prints each plan item with its position and the total (for example "item X: 184 of 203"). Every quoted queue position would come from that output instead of hand counts of the order line. Until it exists, a rule: take any quoted position from Athena's output, never from counting tokens.
proposed_request: Add a per-item plan view to Athena's status output. For each item in the plan, show its position, the total number of items, its job id, its state and its priority. Add a lookup that takes an item id and returns its position and the total. Tests: a plan with separators between items gives positions that count items only; an id that is not in the plan reports that it is absent. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
